q: Average stock = Rs. 12,000; closing stock is Rs. 3,000 more than the opening stock. The value of closing stock is ____

q: If you deposit Rs.10,000 today at 12% rate of interest, in how many years will this amount grow to Rs. 80,000. Work out by using the rule of 72.
e: The correct answer is 18 years. by the Rule of 72, doubling time = 72 ÷ interest rate = 72 ÷ 12 = 6 years per doubling. Rs. 10,000 → 80,000 needs 3 doublings (10k→20k→40k→80k), i.e., 3 × 6 = 18 years. Related exam fact: the Rule of 72 gives a quick estimate of compound-growth doubling time. The principle behind this is worth grasping, not just memorising: once you understand why the rule is framed this way, the answer follows naturally instead of needing rote recall.
